summary: In the hovercraft, Tank is searching the Matrix when Trinity asks what just happened; Tank answers that he doesn't know and has lost him. Morpheus begins to say that "he's on the run" when a siren suddenly sounds, prompting Tank to curse, and Morpheus bolts to the ladder.

what_changes.before: He is tracking someone in the Matrix, then loses him.
what_changes.after: He no longer knows where the person is.
what_changes.evidence:
TANK
I don't know.  I lost him.

what_changes.before: He is speaking, interpreting what is happening.
what_changes.after: He reacts to the siren by rushing to the ladder.
what_changes.evidence:
Suddenly, a SIREN SOUNDS.
TANK
Oh shit

event_hint.one_line: The crew loses track of Neo in the Matrix, then an alarm interrupts them as Morpheus rushes to the ladder.

uncertain: What the siren is warning about.
Whether Morpheus reaches the ladder or why he goes there.

minds.wants: To locate Neo on the screen and report his status back to the crew.
minds.feels: A professional's alarm spiking into genuine fear — he has just watched Neo nearly killed (sc-183) and now the visual feed has gone dark at the worst possible moment, and the siren tells him the reason may be that their own ship is now the target.
minds.shows: Only the one word that breaks past discipline — 'Oh shit!' — before he presumably returns to his task. The curse is the crack in the operator's composure.
minds.basis: He reports 'I lost him' (the tracking failure), then the SIREN sounds and his single line 'Oh shit!' is the only emotional leak; the event shape says the siren signals incoming Sentinels, so his curse is a recognition of a new, lethal threat, not just losing the feed.

believes_about.belief: That losing him on-screen means he is unaccounted-for and possibly caught, not that he has escaped.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is in fact fleeing toward an exit (the hotel phone), but the feed cut has erased him from Tank's sight, so Tank can only register the worst-case absence.

minds.wants: To understand what she just witnessed — Neo apparently being killed — and to get a read on whether he is still alive.
minds.feels: Dread she has no room to express; she just saw Neo coughing blood with wild life-signs (sc-183), and now the crew's attention is being ripped away from him by the alarm, leaving her with no answer at the moment she most needs one.
minds.shows: A plain question, 'What just happened?' — framed as a request for information so it can be answered, not as the panic it also is.
minds.basis: Her line follows immediately after sc-183, where she cried 'Jesus, he's killing him!' watching Neo's body jerk and cough blood; her question here is the continuation of that horror, and no one actually answers it before the siren cuts them off.

believes_about.belief: That he is about to give her an interpretation ('He's on the run --') that will settle the question.
believes_about.wrong_because: He cannot finish it — the siren interrupts, and whatever reassurance she hoped for is replaced by an emergency that redirects all of them.

minds.wants: To make sense of the chaos for the others and to get to his post the instant the ship's alarm sounds.
minds.feels: The quick, unconflicted shift of a commander: he reads the situation ('He's on the run'), then the siren instantly reorders his priorities to the defense of the ship, with no wasted motion or visible doubt.
minds.shows: The interrupted sentence 'He's on the run --' and then pure physical response — he bolts to the ladder. He lets nothing else show; the body does the deciding.
minds.basis: He begins an interpretive statement and is cut off by the SIREN, then immediately 'bolts to the ladder'; the event shape identifies this as the Sentinel-attack protocol, so his movement is trained, pre-decided action, not confusion.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is 'on the run' and therefore still in the fight and reachable — a commander's working assumption meant to steady the crew.
believes_about.wrong_because: He states it as fact but has no confirmation; within the larger event Neo is about to be shot and killed (ev-034), so Morpheus's read is both hopeful and, for the moment, unfalsified.

believes_about.belief: That she can be steadied by being given an interpretation rather than by reassurance.
believes_about.wrong_because: He never gets to test this — the siren ends the exchange before his words can land on her.

connects_back: Trinity's 'What just happened?' is the direct continuation of her horror in sc-183 watching Neo's body jerk and cough blood.
Tank 'losing him' follows the subway fight (sc-182/184) where Neo's movement and the train's passage would break line-of-sight tracking.
The SIREN is the first sign of the Sentinel attack named in ev-033, which the crew could not yet see coming in the subway scenes.
sets_up: The shift of all attention from Neo to the ship's defense, which is why Neo's flatline (ev-034) happens while the crew is occupied elsewhere.
Morpheus moving to the ladder/EMP station, enabling the EMP discharge that clears the Sentinels (ev-035).
The urgency that forces the crew to locate and use an exit quickly, leading to Neo being pulled out (ev-035).
dramatic_function: It pivots the entire sequence from a single combat in the Matrix to a two-front crisis, yoking Neo's fate to the ship's survival and using the siren to sever Trinity's question unanswered — so that the personal stakes (is Neo alive?) and the tactical stakes (the Sentinel attack) collide and neither can be resolved before the other demands action.
